software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.student_educational_license_commitment: Core production software is accessible via official educational licensing programs at zero software cost for enrolled students. Autodesk AutoCAD and Autodesk 3ds Max 2027 provide renewable 1-year educational licenses via the Autodesk Education Community. Epic Games Twinmotion 2026.1 and Unreal Engine 5.8 are free for educational learning and creative individuals. Blender 5.1+ is 100% free and open-source under GNU GPL. Chaos Group provides deeply subsidized student educational licensing for Chaos V-Ray 7 and Corona. Adobe Photoshop is accessed via standard student Creative Cloud plans or institutional lab suites.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.hardware_and_workstation_baseline: Curriculum exercises are engineered for standard high-performance student laptops and desktop workstations running 64-bit Windows 11 Pro. Minimum hardware baseline requires an 8-Core modern CPU (Intel Core i7/i9 13th-15th Gen or AMD Ryzen 7/9 7000/9000 series), 32 GB RAM (64 GB strongly recommended for multi-million polygon V-Ray and UE5 Nanite scenes), dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX GPU (RTX 3070 / 4070 / 4080 with minimum 12 GB VRAM) for OptiX AI denoising, V-Ray GPU, Lumen hardware ray tracing, and Twinmotion path tracing, and a 1 TB NVMe SSD for fast local asset caching.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.zero_cost_asset_library_commitment: 100% of mandatory student assessments and portfolio capstones utilize bundled, zero-cost asset libraries. Primary ready-to-render 3D models and PBR materials are sourced directly through Chaos Cosmos (included free with Chaos V-Ray) and Quixel Megascans / Fab (free educational access integrated in Twinmotion and Unreal Engine). The course requires ZERO purchases of commercial third-party plugins (such as Forest Pack Pro or RailClone Pro); all parametric scattering and asset distribution are taught using built-in 3ds Max tools, Chaos Scatter, and Twinmotion native foliage systems.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.responsible_ai_usage_policy: AI assistance tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Adobe Firefly) are integrated as workflow accelerators for design brief deconstruction, PBR material specification, Python draft generation, and 2D visual moodboarding. Strict academic governance mandates that AI-generated imagery serves exclusively as 2D conceptual reference and texture inspiration; generated 2D images NEVER substitute for dimensionally accurate, editable, structurally valid 3D architectural geometry.

mcp_security_and_sandboxing_policy.blender_mcp_supervision_level: Blender Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration is classified as ADVANCED SUPERVISED EXPOSURE only. It is strictly non-mandatory for course completion and is never deployed for unmonitored student access.
mcp_security_and_sandboxing_policy.sandbox_isolation_requirement: All MCP server-agent communications must execute strictly within an isolated, sandboxed environment (Docker container or virtualized test lab profile) with locked filesystem boundaries and local loopback (127.0.0.1) network bindings.
mandatory_security_rules: Zero unreviewed code execution: Every Python script or JSON-RPC tool call generated by an AI agent must be manually reviewed and approved by an instructor before execution in Blender.
Zero client or proprietary data exposure: No commercial client drawings, confidential project models, or proprietary assets may be exposed to external LLM agent contexts.
Zero credential exposure: No personal credentials, system API keys, or institutional passwords may be stored or accessible within the agent environment.
Zero unrestricted internet access: The MCP execution container must have outbound internet access blocked, restricting communication strictly to the local loopback interface.

Zero production workstation installation: Experimental MCP servers and background listener daemons are strictly prohibited from being installed on primary studio production machines running client-facing commercial software.
mcp_security_and_sandboxing_policy.graceful_fallback_workflow: If an isolated classroom sandbox cannot be established on a student workstation, teaching for Module 15 defaults seamlessly to instructor-led, pre-recorded offline demonstrations and pre-validated manual Python scripts.

faq.q: Who can join the Architectural Visualisation Master program?
faq.a: The program is designed for beginners interested in architectural rendering, interior design students and practitioners, architecture graduates, 3D generalists, and CAD drafters seeking career-mastery training in commercial architectural visualization.

faq.q: Is an architecture degree required to enroll or work in ArchViz?
faq.a: No. An architectural degree is not required. The course teaches architectural drawing interpretation, plan reading, elevation scaling, and architectural standards from foundational principles directly within the curriculum.

faq.q: Is AutoCAD included in the training?
faq.a: Yes. Module 02 provides 26 dedicated guided hours on architectural AutoCAD drafting, blueprint cleanup, dimensioning, layers, blocks, Xrefs, and CAD-to-3D preparation workflows.

faq.q: Is Autodesk 3ds Max 2027 included in the curriculum?
faq.a: Yes. Autodesk 3ds Max 2027 serves as the primary 3D modeling and scene assembly platform, spanning architectural modeling (Module 03), furniture modeling (Module 04), scene optimization (Module 05), materials (Module 06), cameras/lighting (Module 07), and rendering (Module 08).

faq.q: What V-Ray version is supported in the course?
faq.a: The program is developed on Chaos V-Ray 7 for 3ds Max, covering V-Ray Physical Cameras, VRaySun/Sky, HDRI dome lighting, photometric IES luminaires, PBR material shaders, V-Ray Frame Buffer 2 (VFB 2), interactive LightMix, and multi-channel OpenEXR passes.

faq.q: Will students create both interior and exterior architectural scenes?
faq.a: Yes. Students master both interior and exterior visualization: Portfolio Project 01 focuses on a luxury residential interior suite, and Project 02 focuses on a multi-story commercial office building exterior complex with full urban site context.

faq.q: Is realistic lighting taught in depth?
faq.a: Yes. Module 07 (20 guided hours) is entirely dedicated to architectural lighting: natural solar orientation, HDRI image-based lighting, photometric IES profiles for recessed fixtures, cove lighting pelmets, Kelvin color temperatures, and multi-scenario lighting (Morning, Twilight, Night).

faq.q: Are architectural materials and UV mapping thoroughly covered?
faq.a: Yes. Module 06 (28 guided hours) is dedicated to physically based rendering (PBR) material creation, the 3ds Max Slate Material Editor, UVW Map modifiers, procedural dirt/aging, and building a 16-shader architectural material suite across 8 mandatory material categories.

faq.q: Does Photoshop post-production get practical hands-on training?
faq.a: Yes. Module 10 (12 guided hours) provides comprehensive training in Adobe Photoshop 2026: multipass render assembly, Camera Raw color grading, Ambient Occlusion multiply blending, sky replacement, perspective-matched entourage integration, and Z-Depth atmospheric effects.

faq.q: Is Twinmotion included in the program?
faq.a: Yes. Twinmotion 2026.1 is covered in Month 6 across Module 12 (28 guided hours) and Module 13 (12 guided hours), focusing on Datasmith Direct Link synchronization, real-time PBR shaders, procedural terrain, foliage painting, and dynamic animated traffic/people.

faq.q: Will students create cinematic walkthrough videos?
faq.a: Yes. In Module 13, students direct, animate, and export a 30–60 second 4K cinematic architectural walkthrough video at human eye-level (1.50m) as part of Portfolio Project 03.

faq.q: What Unreal Engine skills are covered in the course?
faq.a: Module 14 (18 guided hours) introduces Unreal Engine 5.8 ArchViz fundamentals: Datasmith DCC ingestion, Nanite virtualized micro-polygons, Lumen dynamic global illumination, architectural Material Instances, Cine Camera Sequencer animations, Movie Render Queue exports, and basic Blueprint interactivity.

faq.q: Is Blender included in the program?
faq.a: Yes. Blender 5.1+ is taught in Module 15 (22 guided hours), focusing on procedural architectural modeling using Geometry Nodes and non-destructive scene auditing scripting via the Blender Python API (`bpy`).

faq.q: What are Geometry Nodes and how are they used in ArchViz?
faq.a: Geometry Nodes is Blender's procedural modeling framework. In this course, students use Geometry Nodes to build parametric architectural elements such as facade louvers, solar shading fins, modular cladding panels, and railings that update dynamically based on user parameters.

faq.q: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in Blender?
faq.a: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open client-server architecture that enables AI desktop assistants to communicate with applications. In Module 15, students study how an AI client communicates with a Blender add-on socket to query scene metadata.

faq.q: Are MCP laboratory exercises safe to run?
faq.a: Yes, because the lab is strictly governed by our 16-point Mandatory Safe Lab Design protocol. The training runs exclusively in instructor-controlled, isolated virtual machines with disabled network egress and snapshot rollback verification. Live unguarded execution on production or personal computers is strictly prohibited.

faq.q: Do students need prior programming or coding knowledge?
faq.a: No prior programming experience is required. Python scripting in Module 15 is taught from foundational principles, focusing on simple, readable scene inspection scripts (reading object counts, polygon stats, and missing materials) rather than complex software engineering.

faq.q: Are commercial software licenses included in the course fee?
faq.a: The course fee covers instructional training, guided lab access, learning materials, and project mentorship. Commercial perpetual software licenses are not included. Students are guided to set up official educational, trial, or free licenses provided by Autodesk, Chaos Group, Epic Games, and Blender.

faq.q: What computer hardware or GPU is necessary to participate?
faq.a: Recommended student hardware: Windows 11 PC, 8-Core CPU (Intel i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 7/9), 32GB+ RAM (64GB optimal), dedicated NVIDIA RTX GPU (RTX 3070, 4070 or higher with 12GB+ VRAM), and 1TB NVMe SSD. Windows is required for 3ds Max.

faq.q: Can students use institute lab computers for their practical work?
faq.a: Yes. Enrolled classroom students have access to institute computer workstations during scheduled lab sessions. Remote and online students complete practical assignments on their personal workstations meeting the hardware prerequisites.

faq.q: How many portfolio projects do students complete during the program?
faq.a: Students complete four major mandatory portfolio projects: (1) Photorealistic Residential Interior Suite, (2) Commercial Architectural Exterior Complex, (3) Real-Time Architectural Walkthrough & Presenter, and (4) Advanced Real-Time / Procedural Showcase.

faq.q: Is a real paid-client project guaranteed during the course?
faq.a: No. We do not guarantee real paid commercial client projects. All four portfolio capstone projects are structured as realistic commercial studio simulations based on professional architectural briefs, CAD blueprints, and design criteria.

faq.q: What is the total duration and guided instructional hours of the course?
faq.a: The course duration is 8 Months, comprising exactly 17 Modules and 320 guided instructional and lab hours (40 guided hours per month).

faq.q: What is the tuition fee for the Architectural Visualisation Master program?
faq.a: The approved institutional tuition fee is INR 69,900. Nova Skills operates a transparent pricing policy with zero fabricated discounts.

faq.q: Is Goods and Services Tax (GST) included in the price or extra?
faq.a: Statutory 18% GST (INR 12,582) is applicable over the base tuition fee, bringing the total fee to INR 82,482. Transparent tax invoices are provided upon enrollment.

faq.q: Are flexible installment or EMI payment plans available?
faq.a: Yes. Flexible EMI financing plans are available through approved institutional financial partners, subject to student credit eligibility and partner verification.

faq.q: What career and placement support is verified by the institute?
faq.a: Verified career support includes professional portfolio curation on Behance and ArtStation, 16:9 executive presentation deck design, technical interview troubleshooting defense, freelance proposal and quotation templates, and industry portfolio reviews. Job placement or guaranteed salaries are not promised.

faq.q: Does this course teach architectural engineering, civil structural analysis, or municipal sanctions?
faq.a: No. This program is dedicated to 3D visual communication, architectural cinematography, photorealistic rendering, and real-time visualization. It does NOT teach structural engineering, civil drafting, MEP engineering, or municipal building permit certifications.

faq.q: How is this course different from the 3D Visualisation Professional program?
faq.a: The 3D Visualisation Professional program is a shorter foundational course covering basic 3D modeling and rendering. The Architectural Visualisation Master is an intensive 8-month, 320-hour career mastery program covering complete architectural CAD-to-render pipelines, Chaos V-Ray 7, Twinmotion real-time walkthroughs, Unreal Engine 5.8, Blender Geometry Nodes, Python auditing, and four comprehensive commercial portfolio capstones.

mcp_safety_specification.vulnerability_warning: The Blender Foundation MCP server allows execution of arbitrary Python scripts inside Blender. Unguarded execution poses severe risks of data corruption, system compromise, and unauthorized file access.
prohibited_environments: Student personal computers containing personal documents or credentials
Network storage shares containing commercial client projects
Environments with active cloud API keys or database credentials
Workstations with unrestricted host filesystem access
mandatory_safe_lab_design: 1. Instructor-controlled isolated Virtual Machine (VM) execution only
2. Disposable copies of architectural scenes exclusively
3. Zero personal files or student data inside the VM
4. Zero sensitive commercial client assets present
5. Zero production credentials, tokens, or API keys
6. Zero privileged access from VM to host operating system
7. Restricted or disabled outbound network connectivity (air-gapped preferred)
8. No shared host folders containing sensitive or production files
9. Mandatory VM snapshot recorded before every executable lab
10. Only teacher-approved tools, scripts, and endpoints permitted
11. Every write/mutation action requires explicit, documented instructor approval
12. Mandatory line-by-line human review of generated Python code prior to execution
13. Continuous logging and inspection of all tool calls and console output
14. Mandatory VM rollback to clean snapshot following completion of risky exercises
15. Strict prohibition against automatic approval of AI-generated agent scripts
16. Strict prohibition against unsupervised or autonomous execution loops
mcp_safety_specification.read_only_guarantee_notice: The Blender Lab MCP server does NOT provide an inherent cryptographic or OS-level read-only guarantee. Natural-language prompt instructions ('run in read only mode') DO NOT prevent destructive execution. Process and filesystem boundaries must be enforced independently at the operating system and VM level.
mcp_safety_specification.live_execution_status: BLOCKED unless all 16 mandatory VM isolation, network segmentation, and snapshot prerequisites are verified by the instructor.
mcp_safety_specification.approved_educational_fallback: When isolated VM prerequisites cannot be confirmed, live MCP connections are strictly prohibited. The class implements the approved non-executable educational alternative: static architecture diagrams, recorded safe demonstration videos, line-by-line reviewed offline Python scripts, and manual disposable scene inspection labs.
